data_facts_with_vis_data_meta.paragraph: In Sweden, it is estimated that approximately 8,000 people are living with HIV, with approximately 400–500 new cases each year. In 2019 men accounted for 64% of new cases, with 38 years of age being the mean age at diagnosis. Overall, Sweden has a relatively low HIV prevalence rate and in 2016 was the first country to officially achieve UNAIDS and WHO’s 90-90-90 targets. This has been attributed to policies such as the Communicable Diseases Act, providing antiretrovirals free of cost, high levels of ART adherence, and using interdisciplinary care teams within specialty HIV clinics.
